findings.body: The `mongod` service gets both the entrypoint shim and `GLIBC_TUNABLES`, while `mongo-secrets` gets only `GLIBC_TUNABLES`. The file's own comment says the image "hard-refuses to start `mongod`" on affected kernels and that the shim only "stops the image refusing to start" while the tunable is the real mitigation. If `mongo-secrets` runs the same MongoDB community-server image (which setting `GLIBC_TUNABLES` on it suggests), it would also hit the startup refusal and need the entrypoint override and the volume mount for the bypass script. I could not read the base `docker-compose.yml` to confirm what image or command `mongo-secrets` uses, so this depends on that unseen detail.
findings.title: Apply the entrypoint bypass to mongo-secrets if it shares the mongod image

value.summary: This overlay adds a kernel-bypass compose file for local development on newer Linux kernels, overriding the mongod entrypoint with a shim and setting GLIBC_TUNABLES on two services. The change looks reasonable, but I could not verify the base docker-compose.yml to confirm that mongo-secrets uses the same image and therefore also needs the entrypoint bypass rather than just the tunable.
